description: The ride starts in the hero. Choosing a business type no longer scrolls anywhere: the sign, band and search dissolve in place and page 1 materializes in the same hero frame, then four pages crossfade there - The problem, Why it matters (two reasons, each with a 'what changes' line, plus booking), Your Virtual helper (lead-in, role, three catches, overflow line; ends in two doors), and Wrap up as either the calculator or the booking summary. Every page has Escape; the wrap-up has Get off the ride. Carousel stays behind the Virtual Roles nav tab. New hero copy is Eric's verbatim: 'Choose your business type here.' with his sub-line. Schema v2 gains two optional fields (reasons[].help, role.lead) with a derived fallback so all 8 reviewed entries render today.

approvedBuild.note: 011 remains the approved build. Baselines committed: 012 (6577154), 013 (9c01cd6). 014 (band+blur) and 015 (the ride) are uncommitted and need Eric's eyes-on review.

qa.note: Playwright, tests/dassa-qa.spec.js, rewritten for the ride (39 tests x 7 viewport projects), run 2026-09-22: 199 passed, 0 failed, the rest skipped by design (pointer-only / touch-only). Verified: no document scroll on choose from search, band chip, or the below-fold carousel CTA (which scrolls to the top first, then rides); page 1 fits the viewport with no internal scroll on desktop and tablet (phones may scroll inside a page, never the document); the sign pulses then settles and is static under reduced motion; page 2 shows two reasons each with a help line; the two doors on page 3; honest fallback skips page 2 and hides the HIPAA note; deep links to every page land at scrollY 0; browser back walks the rail; escape restores the sign and clears the search; Get off the ride keeps the search value without reopening results; the sign layer is inert while riding; rail has the four exact labels. Detector 31. Still needs Eric: the materialize and the sign as perceived on his own screens, the hero now filling the desktop viewport at rest, and the page-3 booking button decision.
